title.en: Practical 3: Resistivity of the material of a wire

text.en: Using a voltmeter, an ammeter and a screw gauge, you can find what a wire is made of in terms of its resistivity.

The aim is to determine the resistivity of the material of a coil of wire. The equipment is a coil of wire, screw gauge, metre scale, battery, key, ammeter, voltmeter, rheostat and connecting wires.
Connect the battery, ammeter, wire, rheostat and key in series, and the voltmeter in parallel with the wire. Adjust the rheostat for currents of 0.5 A, 1.0 A, 1.5 A and so on and note the potential difference each time; resistance R = V / I. Measure the wire's diameter with the screw gauge and its length with the metre scale.
Radius r = diameter / 2, area A = pi r squared, and resistivity = R A / L in ohm metre. Take the mean of the resistance values.
